source: "Create a massive, floating stone arena inspired by the Dragon Ball Super Tournament of Power. The world is set in an infinite cosmic void with glowing nebulae, floating celestial platforms, shifting dimensional colors, and high-tech energy pillars surrounding the arena. Make the atmosphere feel boundless, hyper-cosmic, and transcendent with dramatic lighting."

image_prompt.text: The open carved-stone rim of the arena falling away into the cosmic void, so being driven to the edge is a real risk
Tall high-tech energy pillars standing around the arena floor, breaking sight lines for a retreating fighter
Fighter entry points set back toward the arena rim, screened by the energy pillars
Smaller floating celestial platforms scattered around the main arena at varying heights and distances
An infinite cosmic void backdrop of glowing nebulae, stars and shifting dimensional colours

layout_placement.text: Fighter spawns placed apart on the arena floor so nobody appears inside another player's reach

notes: Most of the prompt describes the surround rather than the clash space; the floating platforms and nebulae are carried as unmatched image entries.

Whether the smaller floating platforms are playable was not stated. They are drawn as backdrop, which is the cheaper reading; making them playable would push the shape toward arena-stacked and add P2.

open_questions.ask: Are the smaller floating platforms fightable ground, or backdrop only? Fighting on them makes this a multi-level arena and a slower build.
Is the win condition ring-out, last-one-standing, or a timed tournament bracket?

coverage_missing.ask: Are the smaller floating platforms fightable ground, or backdrop only?
Is the win condition ring-out, last-one-standing, or a timed tournament bracket?
How wide should 'massive' be — a single readable arena, or big enough that fighters can lose each other?

answers.ask: Are the smaller floating platforms fightable ground, or backdrop only? Fighting on them makes this a multi-level arena and a slower build.
answers.answer: The smaller floating celestial platforms are backdrop only; keep all playable combat on the main floating stone arena.

answers.ask: Is the win condition ring-out, last-one-standing, or a timed tournament bracket?
answers.answer: Use ring-out as the win condition, matching the Tournament of Power-inspired arena.
